title: 0/1 Knapsack Maximum Value
description: Each item has a positive weight and value and may be selected at most once. Given parallel arrays `weights` and `values` and a capacity, return the maximum total value whose selected weights do not exceed the capacity.
hints: Define a state by the capacity or sum achievable after processing a prefix.
For 0/1 choices, update capacities in descending order so an item is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int knapSack(int[] w,int[] v,int c) { int[] d=new int[c+1];for(int i=0;i<w.length;i++)for(int x=c;x>=w[i];x--)d[x]=Math.max(d[x],d[x-w[i]]+v[i]);return d[c];} }

title: Rod Cutting
description: `prices[i]` is the price of a rod piece of length `i + 1`. A rod of length `n` may be cut into any number of integer-length pieces. Return the maximum obtainable total price.
hints: Define a state by the capacity or sum achievable after processing a prefix.
For 0/1 choices, update capacities in descending order so an item is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int cutRod(int[] p,int n) { int[] d=new int[n+1];for(int len=1;len<=n;len++)for(int k=1;k<=len;k++)d[len]=Math.max(d[len],p[k-1]+d[len-k]);return d[n];} }

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
description: Return true if the array can be split into two subsets whose sums are equal. Each array element must belong to exactly one subset.
hints: Define a state by the capacity or sum achievable after processing a prefix.
For 0/1 choices, update capacities in descending order so an item is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public boolean canPartition(int[] a) { int sum=0;for(int x:a)sum+=x;if(sum%2!=0)return false;int t=sum/2;boolean[] d=new boolean[t+1];d[0]=true;for(int x:a)for(int s=t;s>=x;s--)d[s]|=d[s-x];return d[t];} }

title: Target Sum
description: Place either a plus or minus sign before each value in `nums`. Return the number of sign assignments whose resulting sum equals `target`.
hints: Define a state by the capacity or sum achievable after processing a prefix.
For 0/1 choices, update capacities in descending order so an item is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int findTargetSumWays(int[] a,int target) { Map<Integer,Integer>d=new HashMap<>();d.put(0,1);for(int x:a){Map<Integer,Integer> n=new HashMap<>();for(var e:d.entrySet()){n.merge(e.getKey()+x,e.getValue(),Integer::sum);n.merge(e.getKey()-x,e.getValue(),Integer::sum);}d=n;}return d.getOrDefault(target,0);} }

title: Last Stone Weight II
description: Repeatedly divide the stones into two groups whose total weights are as close as possible; the remaining weight is the absolute difference between the group sums. Return the smallest possible remaining weight.
hints: Define a state by the capacity or sum achievable after processing a prefix.
For 0/1 choices, update capacities in descending order so an item is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int lastStoneWeightII(int[] a) { int sum=0;for(int x:a)sum+=x;int h=sum/2;boolean[] d=new boolean[h+1];d[0]=true;for(int x:a)for(int s=h;s>=x;s--)d[s]|=d[s-x];for(int s=h;s>=0;s--)if(d[s])return sum-2*s;return 0;} }

title: Combination Sum IV
description: Given distinct positive integers `nums` and a target, return the number of ordered sequences whose values sum to the target. Different orders count as different sequences.
constraints: The answer fits in a signed 32-bit integer
hints: Use a state indexed by the remaining capacity and the amount of progress toward the required target.
Process each choice in descending capacity order so it is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int combinationSum4(int[] a,int t) { int[] d=new int[t+1];d[0]=1;for(int s=1;s<=t;s++)for(int x:a)if(x<=s)d[s]+=d[s-x];return d[t];} }

title: Ones and Zeroes
description: Choose the largest subset of binary strings whose total number of zeroes is at most `m` and total number of ones is at most `n`. Each string may be used at most once. Return the subset size.
hints: Use a state indexed by the remaining capacity and the amount of progress toward the required target.
Process each choice in descending capacity order so it is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int findMaxForm(String[] a,int m,int n) { int[][] d=new int[m+1][n+1];for(String s:a){int z=0;for(char c:s.toCharArray())if(c=='0')z++;int o=s.length()-z;for(int i=m;i>=z;i--)for(int j=n;j>=o;j--)d[i][j]=Math.max(d[i][j],d[i-z][j-o]+1);}return d[m][n];} }

title: Profitable Schemes
description: There are crimes with corresponding member requirements and profits. Count subsets of crimes that use at most `n` members and earn at least `minProfit` total profit. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007. Each crime may be selected at most once.
hints: Use a state indexed by the remaining capacity and the amount of progress toward the required target.
Process each choice in descending capacity order so it is not reused.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int profitableSchemes(int n,int minProfit,int[] g,int[] p) { int mod=1000000007;int[][] d=new int[minProfit+1][n+1];Arrays.fill(d[0],1);for(int k=0;k<g.length;k++)for(int need=minProfit;need>=0;need--)for(int people=n;people>=g[k];people--)d[need][people]=(d[need][people]+d[Math.max(0,need-p[k])][people-g[k]])%mod;return d[minProfit][n];} }

title: Unbounded Knapsack Maximum Value
description: Each item has a positive weight and value and may be chosen any number of times. Given parallel arrays `weights` and `values` and a capacity, return the maximum total value whose total weight does not exceed the capacity.
hints: Define a state by the capacity, achievable sum, or difference between partial groups.
Process each item with the usage rule in the statement.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int unboundedKnapsack(int[]w,int[]v,int c){int[]d=new int[c+1];for(int i=0;i<w.length;i++)for(int x=w[i];x<=c;x++)d[x]=Math.max(d[x],d[x-w[i]]+v[i]);return d[c];} }

title: Minimum Subset Sum Difference
description: Partition the array into two subsets, using every value exactly once. Return the smallest possible absolute difference between the two subset sums.
hints: Define a state by the capacity, achievable sum, or difference between partial groups.
Process each item with the usage rule in the statement.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int minimumDifference(int[]a){int sum=0;for(int x:a)sum+=x;boolean[]d=new boolean[sum/2+1];d[0]=true;for(int x:a)for(int s=sum/2;s>=x;s--)d[s]|=d[s-x];for(int s=sum/2;s>=0;s--)if(d[s])return sum-2*s;return sum;} }

title: Count Subsets With Given Difference
description: Assign every non-negative array value to one of two groups. Return the number of assignments for which the first group sum minus the second group sum equals `difference`. Equal-valued elements at different indices are distinct choices.
constraints: The result fits in a signed 32-bit integer
hints: Define a state by the capacity, achievable sum, or difference between partial groups.
Process each item with the usage rule in the statement.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int countPartitions(int[]a,int diff){int sum=0;for(int x:a)sum+=x;if(diff>sum||(sum+diff)%2!=0)return 0;int t=(sum+diff)/2;int[]d=new int[t+1];d[0]=1;for(int x:a)for(int s=t;s>=x;s--)d[s]+=d[s-x];return d[t];} }

title: Tallest Billboard
description: Use each rod at most once to build two supports of equal height. Return the maximum possible common height. Rods that are not used may be discarded.
hints: Define a state by the capacity, achievable sum, or difference between partial groups.
Process each item with the usage rule in the statement.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int tallestBillboard(int[] rods){Map<Integer,Integer>d=new HashMap<>();d.put(0,0);for(int h:rods){Map<Integer,Integer>n=new HashMap<>(d);for(Map.Entry<Integer,Integer>e:d.entrySet()){int diff=e.getKey(),s=e.getValue();n.merge(diff+h,s,Math::max);n.merge(Math.abs(diff-h),s+Math.min(diff,h),Math::max);}d=n;}return d.get(0);} }

title: Perfect Squares as Unbounded Knapsack
description: Return the least number of perfect-square positive integers whose sum is `n`. A square number may be used more than once.
hints: Define a state by the capacity, achievable sum, or difference between partial groups.
Process each item with the usage rule in the statement.

solutionCode.java: class Solution { public int numSquares(int n){int[]d=new int[n+1];Arrays.fill(d,n+1);d[0]=0;for(int x=1;x*x<=n;x++)for(int s=x*x;s<=n;s++)d[s]=Math.min(d[s],d[s-x*x]+1);return d[n];} }
